previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath and left lower extremity swelling, found to have an acute exacerbation of chronic diastolic heart failure. She was treated with intravenous and then oral torsemide, resulting in improved symptoms, resolution of edema, and stable kidney function. A previously suspected atrial or ventricular septal defect was ruled out by transesophageal echocardiography, which showed the signal was due to normal blood flow dynamics. Her hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia were managed with continued medications. Given her recent move and lack of home support, she was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation. She was instructed to monitor daily weights and to follow up with her outpatient providers.

The pt is a ___ year-old right-handed woman with a history of
prior CVA, HTN, HLD and DM who presents following a transient

once, involving both eyes, and does not think it moved from one
side to the other.  She was not able to sense even vague 
outlines
of objects or light during this time.  Because of these symptoms
she notes that she started becoming more anxious, began 
breathing
rapidly, and felt slightly diaphoretic.  Shortly after this
started her physical therapist knocked on the door.  She reports
that she was able to get up from the couch, and walk to the 
door,
and had no difficulty using her arms and legs during this time. 
While she still could not see, she notes she was able to get to
the door unaided because she 'knows the path very well' and it
was only a short distance.  The physical therapist was able to
then assist her back to the couch, and they discussed possibly
going to the hospital at that time, but she didn't want to. 
About 2 hours after this started, she notes that she was still
sitting on the couch listening to the television, and she 
blinked
her eyes and she could see the television, but it was blurry, 
and
she couldn't make out the faces.  Very shortly after this,
however, her vision completely returned to normal.  She takes 
her
fingersticks regularly, and reports that before lunch that day 
it
was 125, and the physical therapist took it during this episode
and it was 202.  Earlier that day she does note that she had a
throbbing headache at the vertex of her head, that felt like
someone was 'stabbing her with a chisel.'  She does not usually
get headaches like this.  She also notes that for the last 2
weeks it has hurt to sleep on either side of her head because of
pain on her temples. 

She saw her PCP today, and on discussion of this episode she was
sent urgently to ophthalmology, where it was noted that she had
stable visual acuity, and stable diabetic neuropathy, but no
clear pathology that could explain her current symptoms, so she
was sent to the ED for further evaluation.
 
She reports that she has had 3 prior strokes.  The first 
occurred
in ___, and is also documented in OMR.  At that time she notes
that she was at work, when she suddenly felt as though she lost
her vision.  She was able to walk down the hall, and her 
employer
called ___.  She was found to have left sided weakness, and on
MRI had what appeared to be a right sided watershed infarct, but
with no clear anterior circulation stenosis to explain this
(though she did have occlusion of the left vertebral, and
bilateral PCA stenosis).  Since that stroke she had residual 
left
sided weakness.  She notes that in ___ she was admitted to the
hospital with diaphoresis and chest pain, and was told she had 
an
additional stroke, though was not aware of any deficits from
that.  Finally in ___ she was undergoing cardiac bypass, and 
was
told she had 'a stroke on the table.'  She notes that she was
able to walk independently into the hospital for the surgery, 
but
following the surgery she was no longer able to walk without a
walker, and feels her left leg is worse than her right.  In
addition to the above, she also notes that one year prior to her
first stroke she had a similar episode of complete vision loss 
to
what she experienced this week, that time lasting 4 hours, and
again resolving.  She is not aware of having any headache
associated with the first episode.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ h/o prior ischemic stroke (residual left hemiplegia), 
CAD s/p CABG, HTN, HL, DM2 p/w 2 hour episode of transient

temporal tenderness, shoulder pain, and jaw stiffness, most

[] Transient Visual Loss - The patient's vision appeared to 
improve slightly during the course of the hospitalization. Her 
head imaging evaluating for stroke revealed no evidence of new 
stroke. Her story with temporal tenderness, new headache, 
shoulder pain, and jaw stiffness after chewing were strongly 
suggestive of giant cell arteritis. While her ESR was elevated 
at 59, it was actually  decreased from her prior values (in the 
______). We treated her empirically for GCA with Prednisone 60 
daily with Famotidine for stress ulcer prophylaxis and an 
increase of her Glargine for glucose control. We consulted 
Vascular Surgery for temporal artery biopsy which occurred on 
___. The procedure proceeded without significant 
complications. She was observed postoperatively overnight with 
her medications and diet being restarted. 

Vertebrobasilar insufficiency was also considered as a cause of 
the bilateral vision loss. She has an occluded left vertebral 
artery. However, her bilateral vision loss was not accompanied 
by other focal neurological deficits or change in level of 
alertness, making this diagnosis unlikely. MRI brain showed no 
evidence of stroke. She has no prior history of migraines. 
Although she had a throbbing headache at her vertex prior to the 
onset of bilateral vision loss, migraine is thought to be less 
likely as the cause of her event.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with bilateral vision loss three days ago. 
Question intracranial hemorrhage.

COMPARISON:  ___.  Previously noted MR study dated ___ is
not available on PACS system for direct comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous non-contrast axial images were acquired through the
brain with multiplanar reformations.

FINDINGS:  There is no intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, edema, or shift
of normally midline structures.  There is right frontal and subinsular
hypoattenuation, in areas of known prior infarct involving the ACA and MCA
distribution.  There is no new major vascular territorial infarct.  Remainder
of the brain maintains good gray-white matter differentiation.  Suprasellar
and basilar cisterns are patent.  Ventricles and sulci are minimally
prominent, likely reflecting mild degree of age-related involution. 
Underlying small vessel ischemic disease is likely present.

Paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well aerated.  There are vascular
calcifications in the cavernous carotid arteries.  Globes and soft tissues are
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial process.
2.  Remote infarcts in the right ACA and MCA distribution.
3.  As pertaining to history of visual loss, the occipital lobes appear
unremarkable.

INDICATION:  ___ female with shortness of breath.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest demonstrate moderate
cardiomegaly, slightly improved since ___.  The mediastinal and
hilar contours are within normal limits.  There is subtle prominence to the
left main pulmonary artery.  The lungs are clear.  There is no pneumothorax,
vascular congestion, or pleural effusion.  Aortic arch calcifications are
noted.  Median sternotomy wires appear intact.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute cardiopulmonary process such as pneumonia or congestive heart
failure.
2.  Moderate cardiomegaly.

EXAM:  MRI of the brain.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Patient with brief episode of bilateral vision loss. 
Evaluate for vascular structures.

TECHNIQUE:  T1 sagittal and FLAIR, T2 susceptibility and diffusion axial
images of the brain were acquired.  2D time-of-flight MRA of the neck vessels
and 3D time-of-flight MRA of the circle of ___ obtained. 
Gadolinium-enhanced MRA was not obtained secondary to patient's low EGFR. 
Comparison was made with the MRI and MRA examination of ___.

FINDINGS:  BRAIN MRI:

A chronic right frontal subcortical infarct is again identified.  Chronic
infarct in the right periatrial region is also seen.  There is increased
signal identified in the splenium of corpus callosum.  Subtle areas of
increased signal on diffusion images in the right side of the splenium and the
left occipital region anteriorly adjacent to the splenium appear to be T2
shine-through.  No definite acute infarcts are identified.  There is
mild-to-moderate brain atrophy without midline shift or hydrocephalus.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute infarct.  Chronic right frontal subcortical
infarct.  Increased signal in the splenium of corpus callosum new since the
prior study with some atrophy seen on T1 images suggestive of Wallerian
degeneration likely related to previous periatrial infarct.

MRA NECK:

The neck MRA demonstrates no evidence of vascular occlusion or stenosis in the
carotid and right vertebral arteries.  The left vertebral artery appears only
partially visualized through the mid portion which could be due to small size
or due to diffuse atherosclerotic disease.

IMPRESSION:  Normal appearance of both carotid and right vertebral artery. 
Hyperplastic changes or diffuse atherosclerotic disease in the left vertebral
artery.

MRA HEAD:

The head MRA demonstrates areas of loss of flow signal in the supraclinoid
internal carotid arteries bilaterally, with irregularity of the flow signal in
the left middle cerebral and both posterior cerebral arteries.  This could be
due to diffuse atherosclerotic disease, the degree of which could not be fully
assessed on the MRA examination.  If clinically indicated, CT angiography can
help for further assessment.

IMPRESSION: Diffuse narrowing on the left supraclinoid and bilateral posterior
cerebral arteries and left middle cerebral artery could be artifactual or due
to atherosclerotic disease.  If clinically indicated, further evaluation can
be obtained with CT angiography of the head.  Left vertebral artery is not
visualized in the intracranial portion.
